beats.hindi_tts: On organized exchanges, a Central Counterparty interposes itself between every buyer and seller via novation, providing multilateral netting and guaranteeing contract performance.
beats.en_narration: On organized exchanges, a Central Counterparty interposes itself between every buyer and seller via novation, providing multilateral netting and guaranteeing contract performance.
beats.en_subtitle: Central Counterparties (CCPs) novate contracts, guaranteeing zero counterparty default risk.

leftPoints: Legal counterparty to every trade via novation
Multilateral netting reduces total credit exposure
Mutualized default fund absorbs member insolvency
rightPoints: Direct credit risk between trading institutions
Governed by ISDA Master Agreement & CSA
Bilateral collateral thresholds and non-cash haircuts

semantics.teachingObjective: Contrast CCP novation and multilateral netting with bilateral OTC

beats.hindi_tts: In bilateral over-the-counter markets, parties sign an ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex, negotiating bespoke collateral thresholds and accepting securities haircuts.

leftPoints: Daily cash variation margin settlement mandatory
Strict liquidation rules executed next business day
rightPoints: Interest paid on cash collateral held
Collateral posted as pledge, not outright settlement

semantics.teachingObjective: Explain ISDA master agreements and bilateral collateral rules

ui_state.heading: Today's Thread: Core Principles
steps: Margin accounts act as performance bonds ensuring traders never default on futures obligations.
Daily marking to market settles gains and losses each afternoon, resetting contract value to zero.
Maintenance margin is set at roughly 75% of initial margin to provide a safe buffer.
A margin call requires depositing variation margin to restore the balance to 100% initial margin.
Central clearinghouses (CCPs) eliminate counterparty risk through novation and multilateral netting.
Brokers accept Treasury bills at 90% value and shares at 50% value as initial collateral.
LTCM collapsed after $4 billion in losses when extreme leverage met simultaneous collateral calls.
Failing to meet a variation margin call by next morning triggers automatic position liquidation.
